parties.petitioner: The State of Gujarat and others

summary: The State of Gujarat appealed against a High Court judgment directing it to consider the respondents for sympathetic absorption and regularisation, possibly through supernumerary posts, after they worked for seventeen years following initial temporary appointments as drivers in a post-earthquake redevelopment project. The Supreme Court examined whether long service under an interim order justified regularisation, particularly when original appointments were temporary and not in sanctioned posts. The Court found that the High Court overlooked the basis of continuance—i.e., interim orders—and erred in directing absorption, especially via creation of supernumerary posts, which exceeds judicial authority. The appointment was in a temporary project unit without permanent status.
legal_provisions_cited: State of Karnataka v. Umadevi (3), (2006) 4 SCC 1
Narendra Kumar Tiwari v. State of Jharkhand, (2018) 8 SCC 238
final_judgment: Appeal allowed. The impugned judgment of the High Court directing sympathetic consideration for absorption and regularisation, including creation of supernumerary posts, was set aside. The respondents' services to be governed by the interim orders and not regularised.
